claim.text: Closeout receipt 220: the full pytest suite passed at proof-surface source head 03655af9.

control.description: None of its own: the suite's tests are the checks. Changing a fixture byte makes test_v0_1_legacy_fixture_bytes_and_behavior_are_pinned fail.

covers: Whether the suite passes at the recorded head on canonical bytes.
does_not_cover: The working tree the receipt ran in. The receipt records no tree state, so the 721 recorded outcomes against 684 in a rerun cannot be explained from it (ROADMAP T5).
known_result: DRIFT on canonical bytes, measured 2026-10-04: one failure, test_v0_1_legacy_fixture_bytes_and_behavior_are_pinned, because the pin at this commit is the sha256 of the CRLF form of the fixture (3ea68f2c), while Git stores LF (3c6f1865). The suite passes only on a CRLF checkout. proof-surface main pins the LF value (since #32) and marks conformance JSON as binary, so the defect is in this unmerged commit, which sits on no branch.
ci_skip_reason: Known DRIFT on canonical bytes (see known_result); kept as a manifest so the honest result stays one command away. Not run in CI so a known failure does not turn every build red.
setup_note: The setup step installs proof-surface into the interpreter that runs the recheck. Use a fresh virtual environment.
